- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecast often peaks too early and then declines too sharply, missing gradual mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day window, particularly when prices are trending downward.
- Overshoots occur after sharp upward moves in history; model reacts too aggressively, then corrects too quickly.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values in the first 10 days of forecast, then gradually adjusts — but often undercorrects.
- Mean reversion is not adequately captured; model fails to recognize that prices often return to prior 10–15 day averages after spikes.
- Forecast horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly sensitive to recent volatility, underweighting longer-term trends.
- Model tends to ignore or underweight downward momentum in the last 5–7 days of history, leading to overestimation of future prices.
